# ci-compute-github spec

The `spec` block on this engine's entry in `forge-ci.yaml`.

| Key | Type | Required | Means |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | yes | The owner/name the workflows, secrets and runs live on. |
| `dir` | string | no | The repo checkout directory relative to the pipeline root. Defaults to the repo basename. |
| `apiBaseURL` | string | no | The GitHub API base. Defaults to the public API; tests point it at a fake. |
| `tokenEnv` | string | no | The environment variable holding the API token for the run tool. Defaults to GITHUB_TOKEN. |
| `ref` | string | no | The branch dispatches target and pushes land on. Defaults to main. |
| `setup` | list | no | Setup actions run first in every command workflow and the runner, each {uses, with}. The instance names its own toolchain actions; this engine renders whatever it is handed. |
| `workspace` | object | no | The checkout preamble every command workflow and the runner share: bootstrapCommand (one verbatim command that stands the whole workspace up in the working directory, naming its own factory), toolchainScript (verbatim install block). Required once any command workflow or the runner exists. bootstrapCommand is always required; toolchainScript only when spec.container and spec.containerFile are both unset, because an image supplies the toolchain instead. |
| `container` | string | no | The image every job that builds a workspace runs inside, so its tools arrive prebuilt and no install step is rendered. It replaces the toolchain install and not the checkout: an image carries tools, not members, so bootstrapCommand still runs. Fan-out and release jobs never take one - they build no workspace. Empty runs on the runner itself, which is what a factory that PUBLISHES an image needs: a pipeline running inside the image it builds could not publish a fixed one after a bad release. Exactly one of container or containerFile may be set. |
| `containerFile` | string | no | A file under the pipeline root holding the full image reference, tag included - the file a workspace sync generates from its resolved toolchain pin. The alternative to typing the pin into container: the workspace resolver owns the version and this engine only reads it at declare time, so a register-advanced pin reaches the rendered workflows on the next reconcile with nobody editing a pipeline file. |
| `secrets` | list | no | The Actions secrets to seal, each with name and the fromEnv variable its value is read from (default GITHUB_TOKEN). |
| `workflows` | list | no | The owned workflows, each a kind with its parameters or verbatim content, plus an optional header comment block. A command workflow also takes reportFailure (open an issue when a run fails - set it on a workflow nobody watches, meaning a cron run or a repository_dispatch somebody fired from another repo), and pushBranches (also start on a push to this repo, which is how a factory pipeline reruns when its own workspace files change), and pushPathsIgnore (a push touching only these paths never starts the run - the platform's own filter, blind to what a file is for, so list only what nothing embeds). Every command workflow serializes its own runs - one in flight, later starts queued rather than cancelled - because one push wave dispatches once per member, and concurrent applies race the state repo; this is the engine's guarantee, never a knob. Every workspace-building job also restores the tool store from the Actions cache before its bootstrap and saves it under a content-derived key afterwards, so runtimes and toolchain binaries download once rather than every run; also the engine's own behavior, never a knob, and safe because the store rebuilds any entry that no longer matches its description. A release workflow needs a secret too, because it stands the workspace up to reach the toolchain and that clone reaches private members. |
| `phases` | bool | no | Render every command workflow as jobs - self-reconcile, evaluate, one per stage (or per substage, see jobs), release - each running one phase of the apply with --phase, so the run reads as what it is instead of one job named after its first step. The evaluate job answers one word, skip or proceed; every job after it runs only on proceed, so a run with nothing to release shows them skipped. Each stage job uploads what it built as an Actions artifact and the release job downloads them all. A stage named self-reconcile, evaluate or release is refused. Off, a command workflow is one job running the whole apply. |
| `jobs` | string | no | How fine the stage jobs of a phased workflow are cut. stage (the default) renders one job per pipeline stage, its substages running beside each other inside it and its promotion at the end. substage renders one job per substage - the substage and its gates - and one promotion job per stage that needs them all, so a failure and a gate show exactly where they happened. Every job stands the workspace up on its own, so substage costs one checkout per substage. Needs phases: true. |
| `runner` | object | no | The run tool's dispatch target: name, secret, setupScript (verbatim block before the targets), pollIntervalSeconds, timeoutMinutes. Without a name the engine cannot run substages. |

forge-ci never validates a spec. This engine does, because only it knows what the keys mean.
